full_judgment: From the aforesaid definition of "Land" a pond which remains covered with water at any time of the year falls within the definition of land including benefits to arise therefrom. In a decision in the case of Sayeda Khatun and another vs Abedur Rahman and others reported in 1986 BLD (AD) 330 it has been held by their Lordships whether a particular land is non-agricultural land is also to be determined with reference to the user thereof. Both the petitioner as PW 1 and opposite party No.1 as OPW 1 admitted in their deposition that both of them had been using the case land comprising a pond for irrigating water to their crop lands which were contiguous to it. It was thus quite apparent that the case land was being used for the benefit of (agricultural) land. In that context the case land was definitely 'land' within the definition of section 2(16) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and not "non-agricultural land" within the definition of section 2(4) of the Non- Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949. Pre-emption thereof under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was thus quite tenable. Learned lower appellate Court committed an error of law in holding the case land to be non-agricultural land and thereby committed an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.
